rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence yet about whether RNA alone is sufficient or how much profile complexity, learned encoders, image features, aggregation, or fusion matter. This experiment tests a minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline to establish a reference performance and computational cost. It is the best first use of budget because it avoids confounding multiple design choices, is simple and likely stable, and provides a baseline against which later image-only, multiprofile, learned-encoder, aggregation, and multimodal fusion experiments can be interpreted.

The only completed run is a simple RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline (accuracy 0.485, F1 0.464), so there is no evidence yet about whether image features are predictive. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline while keeping the profile setting simple and avoiding aggregation or fusion. This establishes the second unimodal baseline, reduces uncertainty about the modality decision, and will guide whether to invest in image or multimodal configurations rather than assuming fusion will help.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet (0.485 vs 0.208 accuracy; 0.464 vs 0.172 F1), so RNA is the more promising direction. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve the RNA signal. config_002 tests this by keeping the same PCA RNA encoder and adding multiprofile avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect with minimal added complexity. This is a logical exploitation of the strongest result and will clarify whether more complex transformer or multimodal extensions are worth testing.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002), clearly better than RNA-only singleprofile PCA (config_001), while image-only ResNet50 is weak. This makes multiprofile RNA modeling the most promising direction, but the effect of aggregation is still untested because only avgpool has been tried. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed, so it isolates the aggregation decision. This is the best next experiment because it directly extends the current best configuration, tests an important design choice, and reduces uncertainty before committing to more complex multimodal or encoder variations.

Existing evidence shows RNA strongly benefits from multiprofile avgpool (config_002: 0.591 accuracy / 0.573 F1), while transformer and singleprofile are weaker. Image ResNet is only tested as singleprofile and is weak (config_010: 0.208 accuracy / 0.172 F1), so it is unclear whether the image modality is intrinsically weak or simply underrepresented by the singleprofile/no-aggregation setting. config_011 tests the same ResNet image encoder under multiprofile avgpool, the profile/aggregation pipeline that helped RNA, while avoiding simultaneous changes to modality or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about the image main effect before investing limited budget in multimodal fusion; if image improves, multimodal configs become more promising, and if it remains weak, the search can focus on RNA improvements.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA with multiprofile and avgpool is the strongest setting so far (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), outperforming RNA single-profile (0.485) and multiprofile transformer aggregation (0.519), while image-only ResNet models are much weaker. The main uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA without changing the already-promising profile and aggregation choices. config_005 tests scvi_n200 with the same multiprofile avgpool setup, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best direction while efficiently reducing uncertainty about representation before moving to more complex multimodal or fusion experiments.

RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool is the strongest setting so far, and scvi_n200 improves over PCA under that setting (0.650 vs 0.591 accuracy, with F1 following the same trend), but scgpt has not yet been tested. config_008 keeps profile_setting=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool while changing only the RNA encoder to scgpt, isolating the effect of representation under the currently best profile/aggregation setting. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the promising multiprofile/avgpool direction while reducing key uncertainty about whether another RNA representation can beat scvi, before adding image or fusion complexity.

Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile avgpool scvi is the strongest result so far, multiprofile avgpool is better than singleprofile and transformer aggregation, and image-only resnet50 is weak, so the main uncertainty is whether image features can improve the strong RNA baseline. This experiment tests adding the already-tested resnet50 image branch to that exact RNA setting using simple concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodality while preserving the best known RNA representation and aggregation. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest RNA configuration, avoids introducing an untested image encoder at the same time, and directly determines whether further multimodal fusion exploration is worthwhile under the limited budget.

RNA-only scvi_n200 multiprofile avgpool is currently the strongest result (acc 0.650, F1 0.628), while the only multimodal test so far (config_030, same RNA encoder/aggregation but resnet50 concat) is slightly lower (acc 0.632, F1 0.607) and image-only resnet50 is weak. This leaves uncertainty about whether the multimodal shortfall is due to the weak image encoder rather than fusion or the multimodal setup itself. config_036 tests that by replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l while holding RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation, and concat fusion fixed relative to config_030. If it improves, image representation is a key lever and multimodal ViT-L is worth exploiting; if not, image fusion with this RNA setup is less promising. It is a single-change, high-information extension of the best RNA direction and has stronger potential to approach or beat the current best than image-only or fusion-only checks.

The strongest result so far is config_036, a multimodal model using scvi RNA, ViT image features, avgpool, and concat fusion, with 0.715 validation accuracy and 0.687 F1. However, image-only ViT has not been tested, while image-only ResNet was weak, so it is unclear whether the gain comes from the ViT image representation alone or from fusing it with RNA. config_014 tests the image-only ViT setting with the same multiprofile and avgpool choices, providing the missing unimodal baseline. This is the best next experiment because it clarifies whether a simpler image-only model may already be competitive and whether multimodal fusion is actually adding value, which is more informative under a limited budget than immediately testing another fusion variant.
